transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been having some really troubling thoughts lately that I can't seem to shake. It constantly feels like people are watching and monitoring me, and that ordinary things around me have some sort of hidden meaning. My family says these things aren't real, but they feel completely real to me.
Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of depression or periods of unusually elevated or irritable mood?

Yes, I've been feeling really down and depressed for about the last two months, and I've lost almost all my interest and motivation to do anything. I haven't had any times where I felt unusually high-energy, excited, or irritable, though. It has mostly just been this heavy, low feeling.

How long have you been experiencing these troubling thoughts about being watched and things having hidden meanings, and have they occurred at the same time as your depressive symptoms or at different times?

I've been experiencing these thoughts for about eight months now. They've been happening during my depression these past two months, but I also had them before that. There was even a period of a few weeks where I had these thoughts but didn't feel depressed at all.
Have these delusional thoughts or your depressive symptoms significantly impacted your ability to work, maintain relationships, or perform daily activities, and if so, to what extent?

Yes, they've completely disrupted my life. I've lost all motivation to work or even handle basic daily tasks, so I've just stopped doing them. I've also completely withdrawn from my family and friends because I feel entirely disconnected and lack the desire to maintain any relationships.

Have you experienced any notable difficulties with organizing your thoughts, making decisions, or exhibiting bizarre behaviors that are not directly related to your delusional thoughts or depressive symptoms?

Yes, I've had extreme difficulty making even simple daily decisions, like what to wear or eat. My thinking also feels very foggy and dazed, which makes it really hard to keep my thoughts organized. I'm not really sure about any bizarre behaviors, though.
Have you experienced any hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there, in addition to your delusional thoughts and depressive symptoms?

Yes, I've been hearing whispering voices and seeing shadowy figures when no one else is around. Sometimes I even feel strange sensations on my skin or smell things that others say aren't there. It's incredibly exhausting and scary to deal with.
Can you describe the timeline of when these hallucinations started in relation to your delusional thoughts and depressive symptoms, and have they been constant or do they come and go?

The hallucinations started about eight months ago alongside the delusional thoughts, and they tend to come and go. I actually had a period of a few weeks back then where I experienced them without feeling depressed, even though I've struggled with depression off and on for about two years now. Currently, for the past two months, the hallucinations and the depression have been happening at the same time.
Would you say that your depressive symptoms or your psychotic symptoms, such as delusions and hallucinations, have been more prominent and interfering with your life over the past few months?

Both have been extremely difficult to deal with, but the depressive symptoms—like my deep lack of motivation and constant low mood—have felt especially heavy and constant over the past few months. At the same time, the delusions and hallucinations are still very much there and continue to interfere with everything I do.

This concludes the interview. Based on the patient's symptoms and history, a diagnosis of Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) is likely, as the patient has experienced a major depressive episode concurrently with psychotic symptoms (delusions and hallucinations), and the depressive symptoms have been prominent and interfering with their life. However, a definitive diagnosis would require further evaluation and consideration of other factors, including the patient's overall clinical presentation, medical history, and response to treatment.

Thank you, Doctor. Hearing that my depression and these other experiences are connected as Schizoaffective Disorder actually makes a lot of sense given what I've been going through. I really appreciate your evaluation and am completely willing to proceed with whatever further tests or treatment plans you recommend.
